# v0.9.7 evidence: the 32-participant soak's speed

Every figure cites the run that printed it (`[run JOB/RUN:field]`: the run records in
`docs/evidence/runs/`, checked by `tools/evidence/check.py`). Measured numbers only. The soak
also prints two kinds of line that have no run record: its profile (each scope's mean time per
entry between milestones) and its per-kind cost per call in each 30 s window. Figures from those
lines say so (`[unverified: profile line]`, `[unverified: progress line]`), and the lines are
quoted at the end.

**The finding first.** The 2× target is **not met**. Over 600 s the soak slows **6.89×** at
about 97,000 versions (v0.9.5: 10–11×; v0.9.3: 9.9×). From this release the soak's throughput
check is a **regression guard**: at most 8× with the incremental write-back, 8.5× with the old
full write-back. Edits cost about 8× less than in v0.9.3. What still grows with the doc: the
engine's per-edit transaction, blame's map built after each load, and the full-state encode
at each write-back tick and each outside save.

## What was measured, and how

`crates/base/tests/soak.rs`, `soak_32`: 16 people and 16 agents on one doc, release build,
`SOAK_SECS=600`, `SOAK_SEED=1`, `SOAK_KNOWN_D1=1`. The calls (edits, `write --base`, undo,
redo, reads, blame, claims, joins and leaves, outside saves, restarts) come from the seed, so two runs make the same calls in the same order
and differ only in how many fit in 600 s. At every 10,000 versions the soak records the cost
of the 1,000 calls before it, the write-back ticks among them, and the doc's history (the sum
of its state vector's clocks, in UTF-16 units).

**The release gate, job `01e766d0`,** at `a47d616`: the merged v0.9.7 code. The commits from
there to the tag change only comments, formatting, version numbers, docs and tools; nothing
under `vendor/` changes. One x86_64 Linux node with 4 CPUs (`--cpus 4`), `--exclusive`; rustc
1.99.1. The job ran two halves, one after the other, from one build:

- **the incremental write-back** (the default), with `SOAK_MAX_SLOWDOWN=8`;
- **the old full write-back** (`SOAK_FULL_WRITEBACK=1`: each tick re-encodes the doc and
  reloads the disk replica), with `SOAK_MAX_SLOWDOWN=8.5`.

| | Incremental write-back | Full write-back |
|---|---|---|
| Calls in 600 s | 181,011 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:calls] | 163,000 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:calls] |
| Last version | 96,870 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:version] | 87,137 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:version] |
| Restarts | 61 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:restarts] | 55 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:restarts] |
| Calls/s, first 30 s | 1,149 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:first_calls_per_s] | 1,082 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:first_calls_per_s] |
| Calls/s, last 150 s | 167 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:tail_calls_per_s] | 147 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:tail_calls_per_s] |
| Slowdown (%) | **689 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:slowdown_percent]** | **735 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:slowdown_percent]** |
| Most allowed (%) | 800 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:max_slowdown_percent] | 850 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:max_slowdown_percent] |
| Peak RSS (kB) | 189,960 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:peak_rss_kb] | 169,148 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:peak_rss_kb] |

The incremental write-back makes 11% more calls in the same 600 s [derived] and slows less.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.9.3 | `4f451f98` | v0.9.3 | 167,654 [run 4f451f98/soak_32:calls] | 86,903 [run 4f451f98/soak_32:version] | 1,265 [run 4f451f98/soak_32:first_calls_per_s] → 128 [run 4f451f98/soak_32:tail_calls_per_s] | 990 [run 4f451f98/soak_32:slowdown_percent] |
| v0.9.5, at tag time | `00dff865` | `7485a20` | 71,609 [run 00dff865/soak_32:calls] | 38,455 [run 00dff865/soak_32:version] | 554 [run 00dff865/soak_32:first_calls_per_s] → 50 [run 00dff865/soak_32:tail_calls_per_s] | 1,110 [run 00dff865/soak_32:slowdown_percent] |
| v0.9.5, exclusive | `9aa79892` | `8ae359d` | 106,843 [run 9aa79892/soak_32:calls] | 57,406 [run 9aa79892/soak_32:version] | 822 [run 9aa79892/soak_32:first_calls_per_s] → 83 [run 9aa79892/soak_32:tail_calls_per_s] | 996 [run 9aa79892/soak_32:slowdown_percent] |
| **v0.9.7** | `01e766d0` | `a47d616` | 181,011 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:calls] | 96,870 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:version] | 1,149 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:first_calls_per_s] → 167 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:tail_calls_per_s] | **689 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:slowdown_percent]** |

- `4f451f98` ran on the same node as the gate. Its soak had no outside saves yet (they joined
  the soak later), so its workload was lighter.
- `00dff865` ran at two thirds of the exclusive rerun's first-window throughput (554 against
  822 calls/s), so on a busier or slower node; `9aa79892` reran v0.9.5 exclusive, on a node
  of the gate's kind.
- v0.9.7 gets further in the same 600 s (v96,870 against v57,406 for v0.9.5), so its
  slowdown is measured over a larger doc: the comparison does not flatter it.
- **Earlier v0.9.7 gates** on the gate's node, same settings: `0761d991` (`e8c85a6`, before
  the canary's sampling adapted to the doc's history) 686 [run 0761d991/soak_32:slowdown_percent]
  and 702 [run 0761d991/soak_32#2:slowdown_percent] (its check was still 2×, so the records
  are violations); `e1c6891b` (`9d1b41d`) 684 [run e1c6891b/soak_32:slowdown_percent] and
  698 [run e1c6891b/soak_32#2:slowdown_percent]. The canary's changes since then (below) did not
  move the slowdown measurably.

  692 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:milestone_growth_percent]% (to v80k).
- **Per tick** (a write-back), the incremental write-back costs about half the full one from
  v50k on (0.47–0.62× [derived]; 25.3 ms against 54.3 ms at v80k), but it still grows

  text it writes.
- Single milestones are noisy (v80k is below v70k for ticks in both halves); read the trend.

## Where the time goes: the profile per scope

The gate's incremental half: each scope's mean µs per entry over the window before the
milestone (about 9,000 commits and 10,600 engine edits per window), from the profile lines
[unverified: profile line]. The scopes nest: `session.commit` holds `session.apply_local` and
`commit.store`; `session.apply_local` holds `session.prov_build`, `engine.edit_as` and
`session.carry`; `engine.edit_as` holds `engine.txn_ops` and `engine.encode_update`.

| Scope | v10k | v50k | v90k | v90k / v10k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session.commit` | 402 | 743 | 1,161 [unverified: profile line] | 2.9× [derived] |
| `commit.store` | 315 | 400 | 467 | 1.5× [derived] |
| `session.apply_local` | 74 | 308 | 633 | 8.6× [derived] |
| `engine.edit_as` | 18 | 173 | 436 | 24× [derived] |
| `engine.txn_ops` | 9 | 110 | 311 | 35× [derived] |
| `engine.encode_update` | 1 | 1 | 1 | flat |
| `session.prov_build` | 4 | 46 | 119 | 30× [derived] |
| `session.carry` | 33 | 48 | 54 | 1.6× [derived] |
| `engine.canary` (per sample; samples) | 5.2 ms; 7 | 62.1 ms; 3 | 138.0 ms; 2 | 27× per sample [derived] |

- **What grows:** a commit costs 759 µs more at v90k than at v10k [derived]. Of that,
  `engine.edit_as` is 418 µs [derived], most of it (302 µs [derived]) in the engine's
  transaction (`engine.txn_ops`: the inserts and deletes themselves). `session.prov_build` is another
  115 µs [derived]: blame's provenance map is built once per load, O(the history), and the
  soak reloads about every 1,700 edits [derived], so its mean per edit grows with the history.
- **What is flat or nearly so:** encoding the edit's update (`engine.encode_update`, 1 µs),
  the claims carried over the change (`session.carry`), and the store's append
  (`commit.store`, 1.5×).
- The write-back tick, outside saves and restarts are not in these scopes; their cost is in
  the per-tick column above and the per-kind costs below.

## Edits against v0.9.3

Per-kind cost per call in the soak's last 30 s window (to 600 s), from the progress lines
[unverified: progress line], which print µs (written in ms here). The v0.9.7 run is at
v96,870 by then, v0.9.3's at v86,903.

| Call | v0.9.3 (`4f451f98`) | v0.9.5 (`9aa79892`, at v57,406) | v0.9.7 (`01e766d0`, incremental) | v0.9.3 / v0.9.7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| append | 9.06 ms | 8.95 ms | 0.88 ms | 10.3× [derived] |
| insert | 9.36 ms | 7.42 ms | 1.27 ms | 7.4× [derived] |
| delete | 8.55 ms | 9.35 ms | 0.94 ms | 9.1× [derived] |
| write tick | 57.7 ms | 30.0 ms | 46.5 ms | 1.2× [derived] |
| outside insert | (not in that soak) | 177.3 ms | 43.4 ms | |

- **Edits are about 8× cheaper:** 7.4–10.3× in the last window, and 7.0–8.1× averaged over
  the last five windows (the last 150 s) [derived]. One window's figure moves by up to 2×
  between windows (append: 1.68 ms at 570 s, 0.88 ms at 600 s), so the 150 s average is the
  steadier figure. v0.9.5 cost about what v0.9.3 did, on a smaller doc: the drop is v0.9.7's.
- **The write tick is not much cheaper than v0.9.3's** at this size (1.2×), and outside
  saves are 4× cheaper than v0.9.5's [derived] but still cost tens of ms: both encode the full
  state, and an outside save also renders and hashes the doc.

## The canary's sampling

The edit path's canary (a sampled edit is also checked against a throwaway replica, O(the
history)) now samples less often as the history grows past `Config::edit_check_scale_units`
(default 50,000 units). Samples per milestone window, from the profile lines
[unverified: profile line]:

| Job | Commit | What it ran | v10k | v20k | v30k | v40k | v50k | v60k | v70k | v80k | v90k | v100k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `e1c6891b` | `9d1b41d` | the interval scales; each reload restarts the count | 6 | 6 | 7 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 7 | 6 | 6 |
| `e99ef6b7` | `0135f6e` | the next sample one full interval after a reload (scale 200k) | 6 | 6 | 7 | 6 | 6 | 6 | **0** | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| `1699c679` | `cd14ab0` | the first sample after a reload at a phase in the interval (scale 200k) | 6 | 6 | 7 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 5 | | | |
| `a9c25ee0` | `e1ecae2` | the same, scale 50k | 6 | 7 | 3 | 4 | 4 | | | | | |
| **`01e766d0`** | `a47d616` | the release (scale 50k) | **7** | **5** | **3** | **3** | **3** | **2** | **2** | 0 | **2** | |

- **Why the phase fix:** the soak restarts about every 1,700 edits [derived]. At `9d1b41d` a
  reload restarted the count, so the canary ran about once per reload whatever its interval. At
  `0135f6e` a reload put the next sample a full interval away; once the interval passed the
  gap between reloads (from v70k at scale 200k: history
  387,321 [run e99ef6b7/soak_32_v70000:history_units] units, an interval of about 1,900 edits [derived]), the canary **never ran again**: 0
  samples from v70k to v100k. `cd14ab0` places the first sample after a reload at a phase
  spread over the interval, derived from the history, so the long-run rate no longer depends
  on how often the doc is reloaded; the release's gate still samples past v70k.
- **Its cost is not flat:** a sample costs 27× more at v90k than at v10k while the history
  grew 10× [derived], and the release takes 2 samples in most windows from v60k on, against
  about 1 that the interval alone gives at v90k (about 10,600 edits over an interval of about
  14,000 [derived]). Per window that is 36 ms of canary at v10k and 276 ms at v90k [derived]:
  about 3 and 26 µs per edit [derived], small beside a commit's 1.2 ms.
- `e99ef6b7`, `1699c679` and `a9c25ee0` ran on a shared node under load from other jobs, at
  code before D1 (the doc's history at v10k was
  50,373 [run e99ef6b7/soak_32_v10000:history_units] units there, 68,574 in the release); only their sample counts are used here. Their
  600 s ended at v100,123 [run e99ef6b7/soak_32:version], v71,055 [run 1699c679/soak_32:version]
  and v58,840 [run a9c25ee0/soak_32:version] (the blank cells).

## Correctness to call 200,000

Two soaks with no throughput limit, run to 200,000 calls (`SOAK_SECS=3000`, which stops at
the call cap first) at `995bb0f` (the tag's kit code but for comments, the version and a one-line
lint fix), on two other nodes (their timings are not comparable and are not used):

| | `ce73a0c8`: incremental write-back | `73b8d4ff`: full write-back |
|---|---|---|
| Calls | 200,000 [run ce73a0c8/soak_32:calls] | 200,000 [run 73b8d4ff/soak_32:calls] |
| Applied | 95,899 [run ce73a0c8/soak_32:applied] | 95,899 [run 73b8d4ff/soak_32:applied] |
| Last version | 107,123 [run ce73a0c8/soak_32:version] | 107,123 [run 73b8d4ff/soak_32:version] |
| Restarts | 67 [run ce73a0c8/soak_32:restarts] | 67 [run 73b8d4ff/soak_32:restarts] |
| History at v100k (units) | 784,009 [run ce73a0c8/soak_32_v100000:history_units] | 784,009 [run 73b8d4ff/soak_32_v100000:history_units] |
| Position index: lookups / walks / mismatches | 158,583 [run ce73a0c8/soak_32:index_lookups] / 1,180 [run ce73a0c8/soak_32:index_walks] / 0 [run ce73a0c8/soak_32:index_mismatches] | 158,583 [run 73b8d4ff/soak_32:index_lookups] / 1,180 [run 73b8d4ff/soak_32:index_walks] / 0 [run 73b8d4ff/soak_32:index_mismatches] |

- **Both passed with no invariant failure:** the soak's checks held throughout (801
  blame-and-file checks each, 0 known D1 violations, 0 lines written twice), test result ok.
- **The two write-back modes end in the same state:** the same calls applied, the same
  version, the same restarts, the same 6,813 outside saves taken in, the same refusals.
- The gate's two halves also passed every check: 0 known D1 violations, and position index
  mismatches 0 [run 01e766d0/soak_32:index_mismatches] and
  0 [run 01e766d0/soak_32#2:index_mismatches].

## Follow-ups

- **The engine's per-edit transaction** grows with the history: `engine.edit_as` 24× and
  `engine.txn_ops` 35× from v10k to v90k (`engine.encode_update` stays at 1 µs). It is the
  largest growing part of a commit. To the engine team.
- **The full-state encode, and the render and hash,** at each write-back tick and each outside
  save: they go with the incremental stored state, at the next store-format change.
- **The canary's sample count** past the scale is about twice what its interval gives, and a
  sample grows faster than the history; worth a look before the scale is tuned again.
- **The soak's profile and per-kind lines have no run records,** so this note quotes them;
  printing them as `RUNREC` lines would let the checker hold them too.
